title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Y is the (compactified) modular multiplicity or orbifold, e.g. the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν} or its topos. Θ is a normal-crossings divisor, here the boundary, and Y* = Y \ Θ is the open moduli. D' → Y and D'' → D' are 'local immersions', meaning maps that are immersions locally on the source. Typical examples are normalisations of boundary strata, which may self-intersect in Y. On the previous page Grothendieck attaches to any local immersion D' → Y a 'tubular neighbourhood' V_{D',Y}. He defines it intrinsically and topologically, for local immersions of topoi. It is functorial: a composite D'' → D' → Y gives canonical commutative diagrams D'' → V_{D'',Y} → V_{D',Y} → Y.

This page (236). He now brings in the divisor Θ. He pulls Y* back to the tubular neighbourhoods, defining V*_{D,Y} = V_{D,Y} \ Θ_{D,Y}, where Θ_{D,Y} is the inverse image of Θ in V_{D,Y}. This gives V*_{D'',Y} → V*_{D',Y} → Y*, and these are the 'punctured tubular neighbourhoods', i.e. the links of the strata.

The NB records the local structure. V*_{D'',Y} is the complement of a normal-crossings divisor Θ'' inside a tubular neighbourhood of the open stratum Θ''(d0)*. Locally it is a product of the open stratum with a punctured polydisc (C*)^k, and similarly for V*_{D',Y}.

The figure shows a curve, a codimension-1 stratum D', with its tubular band V_{D'}. Inside it are two crossing points, the stratum D'', each surrounded by hatched quadrants. The quadrants are the four local components of the complement of two crossing branches in a small polydisc. The label Θ_{D',Y} points to the pieces of Θ that meet the band.

(237). He then defines the induced morphism of fundamental groupoids Π1 V*_{D'',Y} → Π1 V*_{D',Y}. The fundamental groupoids are not taken with points and homotopy classes of paths as objects and morphisms. Instead the objects are (simply connected) sub-domains and the morphisms are isomorphisms between them. This is the device, also used in the Esquisse, of base 'points' that are contractible regions, for example the quadrants in the figure.

He stresses that this is the advantage of 'localisation': the construction can be made whenever there is a chain of local immersions D'' → D' → Y. No global embedded tubular neighbourhood is needed and no choice of base points.

Purpose. This is part of building the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}. The goal is a system of fundamental groupoids of the punctured neighbourhoods of boundary strata, with transition maps between them. Specialisation from deeper strata to shallower ones should make this a functor on the stratification. The next page announces transitivity for triple composites D''' → D'' → D' → Y. It also announces that the normal-crossings hypothesis will be used to express these Π1's via Π1 of the punctured normal bundles P_{D'*}, i.e. as extensions by Z^k of the stratum's π1.
errors: No mathematical error. The definition of 'tubular neighbourhood for a local immersion of topoi' is only sketched; it is taken from the previous page and not proved there.
The independence of Π1 V* from choices, and its functoriality, are asserted rather than proved.

Using sub-domains and isomorphisms as objects implicitly assumes the domains are connected and simply connected (or at least that the resulting groupoid is equivalent to the usual one). This is not stated.

ideas.what: Punctured tubular neighbourhood V*_{D,Y} = V_{D,Y} \ Θ of a stratum D of a normal-crossings boundary. Its fundamental groupoid is the 'π1 at infinity' attached to the stratum.
ideas.modern_name: link / homotopy link of a stratum; local monodromy groupoid of the boundary of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Topology: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988). Moduli spaces: Ihara, Nakamura and others (boundary fundamental groups of M̄_{g,n}, 1990s). Grothendieck in the Esquisse (1984).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions the 'structure à l'infini' of the Teichmüller tower and boundary fundamental groupoids, but without this construction.

ideas.what: Functoriality of tubular and punctured tubular neighbourhoods for chains of local immersions D'' → D' → Y. This yields specialisation maps Π1 V*_{D''} → Π1 V*_{D'}.
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of links in a stratified space; exit-path / specialisation maps between strata

ideas.what: A fundamental groupoid whose objects are simply connected sub-domains rather than points, with isomorphisms between them as morphisms.
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid on a set of base 'domains'; precursor of tangential base points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (base points chosen as simply connected regions / 'points base' adapted to the cell structure). Also La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois.

ideas.what: Local product structure of the complement of a normal-crossings divisor near a stratum: the open stratum times a punctured polydisc.
ideas.modern_name: local structure of normal-crossings complements; π1 is an extension by Z^k
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Deligne, Hodge II; SGA1 tame ramification, Grothendieck–Murre)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a topos-theoretic, topological definition of tubular neighbourhoods and punctured links for arbitrary local immersions into a topos with a distinguished open. He sets up their functoriality and the induced maps of fundamental groupoids along chains of local immersions. This is essentially the exit-path / homotopy-link formalism for the boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n}, conceived for multiplicities (stacks) in topos language well before Quinn, Treumann and Lurie. The general topos version seems not to have been worked out in the literature as he intended it.
missed.quote: C'est exactement cela, l'avantage de la localisation — nous pouvons la définir chaque fois qu'on a des immersions locales D'' → D' → Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the stratified-homotopy / exit-path description of the boundary of moduli stacks, which is relevant to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller tower and to profinite boundary groupoids. However, the idea is now standard in substance, so the novelty is mainly historical.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent intermediate step: links of strata and functorial maps of fundamental groupoids for the boundary of M_{g,ν}. It uses Grothendieck's characteristic topos-theoretic, base-point-free style. The underlying ideas are now well known, through exit paths, tangential base points and Ihara–Nakamura boundary groups. The page is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.
transcription_corrections: Under Θ_{D'',Y}: read 'image inverse de Θ dans V_{D'',Y}' (not 'ou [?]').
In (237) commentary: likely 'non pas par points et classes de chemins, mais par sous-domaines et isomorphismes entre tels'. The struck word is 'tous', with 'points et' inserted above.
Last lines: 'nous pouvons la définir chaque fois qu'on a des immersions locales D'' → D' → Y' (the [?] is 'locales').
First line (236): the struck-through prefix is a cancelled 'D' / scribble before V*_{D'',Y}, not part of the formula.
